question: What is the primary objective of cancer treatment aimed at complete eradication?
explanation: A cure means the complete eradication of the malignant disease to restore normal life expectancy. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient with widespread metastasis receives care focused solely on comfort and symptom relief. Which treatment goal does this describe?
explanation: Palliative care focuses on relieving symptoms and maximizing comfort when the disease cannot be cured. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: Removing a non-vital organ to prevent future cancer development is known as which type of surgery?
explanation: Prophylactic surgery involves removing at-risk healthy tissue to prevent a malignancy from developing. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why is a wide margin of healthy tissue removed during a curative cancer surgery?

options.A: To promote faster healing of the surgical wound site
options.B: To ensure microscopic cancer cells left behind are excised
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing postoperative pain
options.D: To eliminate the need for any subsequent radiation therapy

explanation: Removing a rim of normal tissue helps guarantee that all microscopic extensions of the tumor are removed. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the term for radiation therapy delivered via implanted radioactive sources close to the tumor?
explanation: Brachytherapy involves placing radioactive material directly inside or adjacent to the tumor site. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h3)

question: A nurse is teaching skin care to a patient receiving external radiation. Which instruction is appropriate to include?

options.A: Wash the marked area gently with mild soap and water
options.B: Scrub the treatment markings vigorously during your daily bath
options.C: Apply heating pads to the skin area to relieve local muscle ache
options.D: Use adhesive medical tape firmly to secure dressings over the site

explanation: Gentle washing protects fragile irradiated skin from breakdown, while friction, heat, and adhesive tapes should be avoided. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary hazard when a vesicant chemotherapy drug leaks into surrounding subcutaneous tissue?
explanation: Vesicants are agents that blister and destroy tissue, leading to severe localized necrosis if extravasation occurs. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h4)

question: What action should a nurse take first when suspecting an intravenous chemotherapy extravasation?

options.A: Document the event at the end of the shift
options.B: Apply firm pressure to the site
options.D: Flush the line with normal saline

explanation: Stopping the infusion prevents any further vesicant medication from entering the subcutaneous tissue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do targeted therapies differ from traditional systemic chemotherapy drugs?

options.A: They work exclusively by increasing red blood cell counts
options.B: They destroy all rapidly dividing cells in the human body
options.C: They only affect patients with localized skin malignancies
options.D: They focus on specific molecular characteristics of cancer cells

explanation: Targeted therapies are designed to interfere with specific molecules needed for tumor growth rather than non-specifically targeting all dividing cells. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which mechanism describes how immune checkpoint inhibitors work in cancer treatment?

options.A: They lower systemic inflammation to keep the patient comfortable
options.B: They directly replace damaged bone marrow cells after high-dose radiation
options.C: They coat the exterior of solid tumors to prevent blood vessel growth
options.D: They help the patient immune system recognize and attack cancer cells

explanation: Checkpoint inhibitors remove molecular brakes on immune cells, allowing T-cells to mount an attack against the tumor. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which oncological emergency features facial edema, jugular venous distension, and respiratory distress?
explanation: Compression of the superior vena cava impairs venous return from the upper body, causing characteristic facial and neck swelling. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary physiological cause of electrolyte imbalances in Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: Rapid destruction of large numbers of tumor cells
options.B: Kidney failure caused by radiation therapy to the pelvis
options.C: Excessive dietary intake of potassium during chemotherapy

explanation: TLS occurs when massive cell breakdown releases intracellular contents like potassium and phosphate rapidly into the circulation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary framework used to guide pharmacological cancer pain management?
explanation: The WHO analgesic ladder provides a stepwise approach for prescribing pain medications based on pain severity. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h7)

question: A patient receiving emetogenic chemotherapy asks when to take their prescribed antiemetic medication. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Wait until you feel severe nausea before taking the first dose
options.B: Only take the medication if you actually vomit twice
options.C: Take it proactively before the chemotherapy session starts
options.D: Take it strictly at bedtime regardless of your treatment schedule

explanation: Prophylactic antiemetic administration is much more effective at preventing chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting than rescue treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h7)

question: When should palliative care ideally be introduced in the cancer care continuum?

options.A: Exclusively when the patient is discharged to hospice
options.B: After all forms of chemotherapy have failed
options.C: Only during the final forty-eight hours of life
options.D: Integrated early alongside active disease-directed treatments

explanation: Early integration of palliative care improves quality of life and symptom management throughout the disease trajectory. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for a patient with advanced cancer?

options.A: Shrinking tumor size through high-dose radiation therapy
options.B: Finding a definitive cure for the underlying malignancy
options.C: Improving quality of life for both patient and family
options.D: Preventing the development of secondary infections

explanation: Palliative care prioritizes comfort, symptom management, and psychosocial support rather than disease eradication. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)
